name: Aerobic granular sludge treatment (Nereda)
applications: municipal wastewater with simultaneous N and P removal
retrofits that need capacity without new tanks
principle: Follows the Royal HaskoningDHV Nereda licensor flow: one cyclical SBR-style reactor with a granular biomass that settles 3-8x faster than flocculent sludge. Simultaneous nitrification/denitrification and bio-P removal happen inside the dense granules (aerobic shell, anoxic/anaerobic core). The published Nereda cycle is: (1) feed/draw from the bottom while decanted clear water leaves the top, (2) aeration/reaction with simultaneous fill, (3) settling of the fast-settling granules, (4) decant of treated effluent; excess sludge is wasted as well-settling granules that dewater easily.

performance.basis: vendor claim: up to 4x smaller footprint

gaps.reason: The IEA guide covers anaerobic digestion but not municipal wastewater process units; no agency TRL exists for most of them. Checked 2026-11-16.

costs.metric: installed capital cost, AGS plus tertiary UF upgrade
costs.basis: Soreq WWTP train 5, 75,000 m3/d basis, built up from equipment costs, membrane quotations and independent review; excludes replacing outdated equipment in existing trains and the new feed pump station. A second case gives 1,758 NIS/m3/d on 79,500 m3/d.

source.note: Giesen et al., Water Practice & Technology 21(8):3544 (2026): 1,863 NIS per m3/d at 75,000 m3/d, 2020 prices, read 2026-11-16
